answer: GUT-1, previously called STNM01, is a CHST15-targeting double-stranded RNA/silencing oligonucleotide that reduces CHST15 expression and is intended to inhibit mucosal inflammation and fibrosis. [S7][S4][S5] In a Phase IIa study of moderate-to-severe left-sided UC, 28 patients were screened and 24 were randomized 1:1:1 to a single injection of 250 nM GUT-1, 25 nM GUT-1 or placebo; participants were aged 18–65 years and recruited from five centres in Germany. The primary endpoint was endoscopic improvement at weeks 2 and 4. [S7][S5] At 250 nM, endoscopic improvement was 71.4%, clinical remission 57.1% and histological improvement 42.9%; the reported placebo rates for those outcomes were 28.6%, 14.3% and 0%, respectively. Endoscopic improvement was 0% at 25 nM. [S7][S4][S5] CHST15-positive areas in the 250 nM arm were 19.7% (95% CI 17.0%–22.5%) at baseline, 11.5% (95% CI 6.5%–16.5%) at week 2 and 8.4% (95% CI 3.1%–13.7%) at week 4, a reported drop of more than 50% from baseline to week 4. In the 25 nM arm, the corresponding values were 19.6% (95% CI 15.2%–24.1%), 14.7% (95% CI 10.6%–18.7%) and 14.0% (95% CI 7.7%–20.2%). [S5] Two hours after injection, plasma GUT-1 was below the LLOQ of 0.5 ng/ml in all treatment groups, and both doses were generally well tolerated. [S5] A Phase I study of STNM01 in 18 patients with Crohn’s disease assessed safety; most recipients had reduced endoscopic inflammation versus placebo, and histological analyses indicated reduced tissue fibrosis. [S10][S5]

label: C
answer:
GUT-1, previously called STNM01, is a synthetic double-stranded RNA oligonucleotide that selectively inhibits CHST15 through siRNA mechanisms. [S1][S2][S5][S6] In vitro, it suppressed CHST15 mRNA dose-dependently and reduced vimentin, α-SMA and Wnt3 mRNA in a TGF-β-stimulated human fibroblast cell line. [S1] A Phase I study of STNM01 in 18 patients with Crohn’s disease found that most recipients showed reduced endoscopic inflammation versus placebo, and histological analyses showed reduced tissue fibrosis; the study demonstrated safety. [S5][S10]

In active UC, the randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2a induction study enrolled adults aged 18–65 with moderate-to-severe left-sided disease refractory to conventional treatment, including patients with prior biologic treatment and endoscopic lesions with MES ≥2. It screened 28 patients and randomized 24 in a 1:1:1 allocation to a single 25 nM or 250 nM dose of GUT-1 or placebo, delivered by endoscopic submucosal injection at five centres in Germany; endoscopic improvement at weeks 2 and 4 was the primary endpoint. [S1][S3][S5][S6] At 250 nM, endoscopic improvement was 71.4%, clinical remission 57.1% and histological improvement 42.9%; at 25 nM, each was 0%; with placebo, the respective rates were 28.6%, 14.3% and 0%. [S3][S5][S6] In the 250 nM arm, CHST15-positive area was 19.7% (95% CI 17.0%–22.5%) at baseline, 11.5% (95% CI 6.5%–16.5%) at week 2 and 8.4% (95% CI 3.1%–13.7%) at week 4. At 25 nM, it was 19.6% (95% CI 15.2%–24.1%), 14.7% (95% CI 10.6%–18.7%) and 14.0% (95% CI 7.7%–20.2%) at those timepoints. Two hours after injection, plasma GUT-1 was below the 0.5 ng/ml lower limit of quantification in all treatment groups; GUT-1 was well tolerated. [S1][S3][S5][S6]

A separate open-label study gave 250 nM GUT-1 by submucosal injection at weeks 0, 2 and 4 to five patients with moderate-to-severe UC who had lost response to maintenance anti-TNF antibody treatment. At week 6, endoscopic improvement was 80% (4/5), clinical response 100% and clinical remission 60% (3/5). Three patients had no clinical recurrence for 52 weeks, and all three corticosteroid-dependent patients had no corticosteroid exposure for at least 24 weeks after achieving remission. [S2]

Other named UC treatments in the evidence include tofacitinib, a JAK1/JAK3 inhibitor approved for moderate-to-severe UC, with efficacy described as comparable to biologics in TNF-α-inhibitor-naive UC and superior to placebo; ozanimod, approved for moderate-to-severe UC and described as most effective for inducing mucosal healing; and PF-00547659, a fully human monoclonal antibody targeting MAdCAM-1 that selectively reduces lymphocyte gut homing in moderate-to-severe UC. [S7] Infliximab is described as having the highest clinical response and remission rates for induction in moderate-to-severe UC. Vedolizumab and ustekinumab are described as favored for safety and gut selectivity after anti-TNF failure or intolerance; in UC, vedolizumab showed higher clinical remission, endoscopic improvement and histological remission than adalimumab in the VARSITY study. [S4][S7]

objective: Inflammatory Bowel Disease competing agents in the same mechanistic class as GPR52 Prostaglandin E2 Receptor EP4, including Small Molecule therapies
answer: NXE0033744 (NXE’744; also HTL0033744/HTL’744) is Nxera’s potent, selective, gut-restricted EP4 agonist for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD); Nxera calls it a first-in-class GI-targeted agent intended to promote mucosal healing. The proposed rationale is combined anti-inflammatory and barrier-repair effects. Nxera says approved IBD agents are immunomodulatory and do not directly target disease-induced mucosal barrier defects, and that current standard-of-care agents have treatment ceilings of about 40% response rates. Previous attempts to agonise EP4 showed early clinical efficacy signals but were limited by systemic safety; no concerning adverse events had been noted for NXE’744 at the time of the R&D presentation. [S12][S13] NXE’744’s Phase 1 trial began with first-subject dosing; Nxera later reported Phase 1 completed successfully, early efficacy signals in an indomethacin challenge study, and Phase 2 readiness. The R&D presentation said activities to support a Phase 1B/II study start were underway, including additional cohorts such as sigmoidoscopy under the FIH umbrella. A January 2025 presentation had planned a Phase 2 study start in H2 2025; a March 2026 presentation instead described the programme as Phase 2-ready. Nxera also said it was in active discussions with six potential partners for a 2026 licence deal. [S11][S13][S19] Nxera’s NXE0027477 (NXE-477) is an oral, highly selective GPR35 agonist for IBD, described as clinic-ready and first-in-class; Nxera regained full ownership from GSK and said it would determine a further-development strategy that could include in-house development or re-partnering. [S12][S13][S15] PF-07054894 is listed as a CCR6 antagonist for IBD, with SME modality. [S19] A separate IBD-relevant EP4 programme reports lead compound 11a, a non-prostanoid, selective EP4 agonist chemotype optimized through structure-activity relationship studies. Compound 11a was profiled in a mouse pharmacokinetic study and showed efficacy in a mouse IBD model; blood exposure induced hemodynamic changes in mice, described as a known on-target effect of EP4 agonists in systemic circulation. [S18]

In orthotopic PDAC mouse models, ADT-1004 significantly inhibited tumour growth in KPC-luc and 2838c3-luc models at 10–50 mg/kg orally, once or twice daily, 5 days per week for 27 consecutive days. In the KPC-luc experiment, mice received vehicle or ADT-1004 by once-daily oral gavage at 10–50 mg/kg, 5 days per week; treatment began on day 0 after imaging and randomisation, and mice were euthanised on day 27 for tumour-growth assessment by bioluminescence and tumour weight. The paper describes this as once daily, whereas MedChemExpress gives once or twice daily. [S11][S14] ADT-1004 also inhibited tumour growth in an orthotopic KRAS G12D PDAC model in C57BL/6J mice at 40 mg/kg orally once daily, 5 days per week for 28 days. [S11] In subcutaneous NSG-mouse PDX models with KRAS G12D, G12V, G12C or G13Q mutations, 40 mg/kg orally once daily, 5 times per week inhibited tumour growth; a treatment duration is not specified. [S11][S14] In NSG mice bearing parental or sotorasib/adagrasib-resistant KRAS G12C PDAC, 40 mg/kg orally once daily, 5 days per week for 31 days inhibited tumour growth. [S11] The study also reports suppressed tumour growth in PDX models with those four KRAS mutations, superior efficacy over sotorasib and adagrasib in models resistant to those inhibitors and MRTX1133-resistant KRAS G12D cells, and no impact on growth of RAS WT BxPC-3 PDAC tumours. [S14] In cell-derived xenograft experiments, MIA PaCa-2, MIA-AMG-Res and BxPc-3 models received vehicle, ADT-1004 (40 mg/kg), sotorasib (40 mg/kg) or adagrasib (40 mg/kg); the BxPc-3 experiment used vehicle or ADT-1004, with n=5 stated for the groups. [S16]
**AACR 2024** ADT-1004 was reported to produce profound tumour regression in animal models, with no impact on body weight; the model, dose and regression magnitude are not specified. [S12]
**EORTC-NCI-AACR 2024** ADT-1004 was administered orally at 40 mg/kg, 5 times per week for 4 weeks; tumour growth was suppressed in KRAS-mutant PDAC models, with inhibition of ERK phosphorylation and no discernible toxicity. [S12]
missing: Model-specific quantitative tumour-growth inhibition, tumour-volume change or regression/shrinkage measurements and criteria; the animal model, regimen and magnitude associated with the reported profound tumour regression; and the treatment duration for the subcutaneous PDX regimen.

label: B
answer: Oral ADT-1004 at 40 mg/kg caused substantial growth inhibition and profound regression of KRAS-G12D and KRAS-G12V tumors, without accompanying body-weight loss. [S7] In PDAC experiments, KRAS-G12D murine cells (KPC-luc or 2838c3-luc) were implanted orthotopically in C57BL/6J mice, and four KRAS-mutant PDAC PDX tumors were implanted subcutaneously in NSG mice; ADT-1004 inhibited tumor growth in these models. [S1][S2] ADT-1004 suppressed PDX tumors with KRAS-G12D, G12V, G12C and G13Q mutations. [S1][S2] A review instead lists G12Q among the responsive mutations. [S5] Doses of 20–50 mg/kg produced comparable statistically significant reductions in tumor weight versus vehicle or 10 mg/kg ADT-1004; oral 40 mg/kg significantly reduced tumor growth by bioluminescence imaging and tumor weight versus vehicle, without differences in body weight. [S1] In orthotopic and PDX PDAC models, daily oral ADT-1004 significantly inhibited tumor growth. [S10] In NSG mice with parental MIA PaCa-2 tumors, ADT-1004, sotorasib and adagrasib were each given at 40 mg/kg once daily, 5 times weekly; each treatment produced comparable decreases in tumor volume and final tumor weight. ADT-1004 also showed greater efficacy than sotorasib and adagrasib in resistant tumor models, including models with MRTX1133-resistant KRAS-G12D mutant cells. [S1][S2][S3] ADT-1004 did not affect growth of tumors from RAS-wild-type PDAC cells, including BxPC3; murine RAS-driven PDAC models also showed robust, durable antitumor activity at well-tolerated doses. [S2][S6]
missing: Exact percentage tumor-growth inhibition and quantitative tumor-regression or shrinkage measurements; the number of animals or tumors that regressed; and model-specific treatment schedules beyond the stated 40 mg/kg once-daily, 5-times-weekly MIA PaCa-2 experiment.

label: C
answer: ADT-1004 treatment significantly inhibited tumor growth in mouse PDAC models. In orthotopic models using KRAS^G12D^ murine PDAC cells (KPC-luc or 2838c3-luc) implanted in C57BL/6J mice, and in subcutaneous KRAS-mutant PDX tumors implanted in NSG mice, most treated mice had reduced bioluminescence versus vehicle; doses of 20–50 mg/kg produced comparable statistically significant tumor-weight reductions versus vehicle or 10 mg/kg. Oral 40 mg/kg also significantly reduced tumor growth by bioluminescence and tumor weight versus vehicle, without differences in body weight. PDX activity was reported for KRAS^G12D^, KRAS^G12V^, KRAS^G12C^ and KRAS^G13Q^ tumors; a review table instead lists KRAS^G12Q^. [S1][S2][S5] An abstract reports that oral 40 mg/kg caused substantial growth inhibition and profound tumor regression in KRAS-G12D and KRAS-G12V tumors, without accompanying body-weight loss. [S7] At oral 40 mg/kg, ADT-1004 also showed antitumor activity in mouse- or patient-derived PDAC models with KRAS^G12D^, KRAS^G12V^, KRAS^G12C^ or KRAS^G13Q^ mutations. [S9] In subcutaneous parental MIA PaCa-2 xenografts in NSG mice, once-daily 40 mg/kg, 5 days/week, produced tumor-volume and final-tumor-weight decreases comparable to those with sotorasib or adagrasib, each given at the same dose and schedule. [S1] ADT-1004 did not affect growth of RAS-wild-type PDAC tumors, including tumors from the BxPC3 cell line described as driven by a downstream BRAF mutation. [S2][S6]
missing: Numerical TGI percentages or tumor-volume reduction magnitudes; quantified regression/shrinkage rates and their definitions; response timepoints or duration; and animal numbers for the reported outcome groups. The KRAS mutation listing differs between the primary article (G13Q) and a review table (G12Q).

label: D
answer: ADT-1004 suppressed tumor growth in orthotopic mouse PDAC models KPC-luc and 2838c3-luc; the KPC-luc model carried KRAS G12D and p53 R172H mutations. In the described KPC-luc experiment, mice received oral ADT-1004 once daily at 10–50 mg/kg, 5 days per week, from day 0 until euthanasia on day 27; tumor effects were assessed by bioluminescence and tumor weight. A separate summary lists 10–50 mg/kg orally once or twice daily, 5 days per week for 27 days, for orthotopic KPC-luc and 2838c3-luc models. [S14][S11] ADT-1004 also inhibited growth in subcutaneous PDAC PDX models in NSG mice carrying KRAS G12D, G12V, G12C, or G13Q mutations; the listed regimen was 40 mg/kg orally once daily, 5 days per week. [S14][S11] In subcutaneous MIA PaCa-2 xenografts, including parental and sotorasib/adagrasib-resistant KRAS G12C models, ADT-1004 inhibited tumor growth; it showed superior efficacy to sotorasib and adagrasib in resistant tumor models. The xenograft study summary lists vehicle, ADT-1004, sotorasib, and adagrasib groups (n=5) and oral dosing at 40 mg/kg, 5 days per week for 4 weeks. [S14][S16][S12][S11] ADT-1004 did not affect growth of RAS-wild-type BxPC-3 PDAC tumors. [S14][S16] **AACR 2024** The presentation claims ADT-1004 produced “profound tumor regression” in animal models. [S12] **EORTC-NCI-AACR 2024** The presentation reports suppressed growth of KRAS-mutant PDAC tumors with oral ADT-1004 at 40 mg/kg, 5 days per week for 4 weeks. [S12]
missing: Numerical TGI estimates and their denominators or statistical comparisons; quantified tumor regression or shrinkage and the specific model(s) in which regression occurred; model-specific tumor-volume and final tumor-weight results beyond the qualitative findings.
